The checkpointer is not relied on, because a re-run may start a new thread. The state that matters lives in the external store.

The tools return clear status, such as 'existing ticket T-881' and 'summary posted', so the trace shows exactly what each run did.
keyPoints: A separate idempotency key per side effect
Re-run returns existing ticket IDs instead of creating new ones
Summary key from channel plus batch date, with pending or done state
External store, not the checkpointer, holds progress
Clear status returns for traceability

subjective.question: Compare a read_sheet tool that returns a plain string with one defined using @tool(response_format="content_and_artifact"). When is the second better?
subjective.answer:
With a plain string, everything the tool returns goes into the model's context. With content_and_artifact, the tool returns a tuple. The first part, the content, is what the model reads. The second part, the artifact, is attached to the ToolMessage but not sent to the model.

The second form is better when your code needs the full data but the model only needs a short view. In this snippet, the model sees the count and complaint IDs and can reason about which rows to ticket. The full rows stay available as the artifact for downstream code, logging or later processing. This saves tokens, lowers the chance of the model picking the wrong record, and keeps bulky or sensitive fields out of the prompt.

A plain string is fine for small, model-relevant results. Remember that whatever the model needs in order to decide must be in the content, because it cannot read the artifact.
keyPoints: Content goes to the model; the artifact stays with the ToolMessage
Saves context and reduces wrong choices
Keeps bulky or sensitive data out of the prompt
Decision-critical facts must be in the content

steps.overview: This step moves your agents out of the chat window. You will run graphs on the Agent Server (LangSmith Deployment) from a schedule (cron job) and from outside events (incoming webhooks), and get a callback when a run finishes. This is the core of the Ambient Agents course: agents that work in the background while humans only review.
objectives: Explain how ambient agents differ from chat agents and when to use schedules or events.
Describe Agent Server assistants, threads, runs and background runs, and how they map to SDK calls.
Create, list, disable and delete a cron job that fires a daily 8 AM IST report using an IANA timezone.
Start the email triage graph from an incoming-email webhook as a background run with a completion webhook.
Tell apart Agent Server run webhooks from LangSmith automation-rule webhooks and alerts.

concepts.explanation: An agent triggered by events or schedules, not by a person typing a chat message. It runs in the background, for example on each new email or every morning. It brings a human in only when needed, usually through an interrupt or HumanInTheLoopMiddleware.

A configured instance of a graph deployed on the Agent Server, identified by assistant_id. The graph name in langgraph.json works as a default assistant. You can create more assistants from the same graph with a different config, such as another model or prompt.
A conversation or work item that holds persisted state across runs. The Agent Server handles the checkpointer for you, so you do not compile with your own saver. Each thread has a thread_id.

A run is one execution of an assistant, either on a thread or stateless. client.runs.create starts a background run that the server's task queue executes; the call returns at once with a run_id. client.runs.wait blocks until the run finishes and returns the final state.

A schedule (cron expression) plus an assistant_id plus an input, created with POST /runs/crons or client.crons.create. Each firing creates a new thread and sends the same input. POST /threads/{thread_id}/runs/crons instead schedules runs on one existing thread.

Schedules are read in UTC unless you pass an IANA timezone such as "Asia/Kolkata". end_time stops the cron after a date. enabled turns it on or off without deleting it. on_run_completed is "delete" (default, removes the thread) or "keep".

An external system, such as an email provider, sends an HTTP POST to a small receiver you own. The receiver maps the payload into graph input and calls client.runs.create. The agent therefore starts with nobody opening any app.

Pass webhook=URL on a run or cron, and the Agent Server calls that URL when the run is done. Use it to post the report to Slack, update a ticket or trigger the next step. It replaces polling the run status.

keyFacts: Cron create endpoint: POST /runs/crons with schedule, assistant_id and input. The Python SDK equivalent is client.crons.
Each cron firing creates a new thread; on_run_completed defaults to "delete", so set "keep" if you want to inspect past report threads.
Cron schedules run in UTC unless you pass an IANA timezone such as "Asia/Kolkata".
8 AM IST = 02:30 UTC. Use "0 8 * * *" with timezone "Asia/Kolkata", or "30 2 * * *" in UTC.
IST has no daylight saving, but zones like Europe/London do. Always pass the timezone for those zones instead of hand-converting.
enabled toggles a cron, end_time stops it, and deleting removes it. Cron and run webhook URLs are called when the run finishes.
POST /threads/{thread_id}/runs/crons schedules runs on one existing thread, so state accumulates on that thread.

LangSmith automation rules (filter, sampling rate, action such as webhook) are a separate system from Agent Server webhooks. A rule meant to fire after scoring should filter on eq(feedback_key, "...").

example.caption: Schedule the 8 AM IST report, list it, disable it, and start triage from an email webhook. Replace the URL with your deployment; set LANGSMITH_API_KEY.
example.code:
import os
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from langgraph_sdk import get_client

client = get_client(url=os.environ["DEPLOYMENT_URL"], api_key=os.environ["LANGSMITH_API_KEY"])

async def setup_daily_report():
    cron = await client.crons.create(
        "daily_report",                       # assistant_id / graph name
        schedule="0 8 * * *",                 # 08:00 every day
        timezone="Asia/Kolkata",              # otherwise read as UTC
        input={"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Build today's report"}]},
        on_run_completed="keep",
        webhook="https://ops.example.com/hooks/report-done",
    )
    for c in await client.crons.search(assistant_id="daily_report"):
        print(c["cron_id"], c["schedule"])
    return cron["cron_id"]

async def disable(cron_id: str):
    await client.crons.update(cron_id, enabled=False)  # or client.crons.delete(cron_id)

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/email-webhook")
async def on_email(request: Request):
    email = await request.json()
    thread = await client.threads.create(metadata={"email_id": email.get("id")})
    run = await client.runs.create(
        thread["thread_id"], "email_triage",
        input={"email_input": email},
        webhook="https://ops.example.com/hooks/triage-done",
    )
    return {"run_id": run["run_id"]}  # returns at once; run is queued

pitfalls: Writing "0 8 * * *" without a timezone gives 8 AM UTC, which is 1:30 PM IST. Pass timezone="Asia/Kolkata" or use "30 2 * * *".
Expecting cron runs to share memory. Each firing makes a new thread. Use the thread-level cron endpoint if you need state to accumulate.
Leaving on_run_completed at "delete" and then finding no thread to debug. Rely on LangSmith traces, or set "keep".
Using runs.wait inside the email webhook receiver. The sender may time out or retry, which creates duplicate runs. Use runs.create and return fast.
Confusing the three webhook features: the Agent Server run/cron webhook (run finished), LangSmith automation-rule webhooks (traces matching a filter) and LangSmith alerts (threshold breaches).
Forgetting to secure the public webhook receiver. Verify the sender's signature or a shared secret before you start a run.

"""Triage graph: started by the incoming-email webhook, never by a chat message."""
from typing import Literal, TypedDict

from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
from langgraph.graph import END, START, StateGraph
from pydantic import BaseModel


class EmailState(TypedDict, total=False):
    sender: str
    subject: str
    body: str
    category: str  # set by classify
    reason: str
    action: str    # set by the routed node


class Decision(BaseModel):
    category: Literal["respond", "notify", "ignore"]
    reason: str


llm = init_chat_model("openai:gpt-4.1-mini", temperature=0)
classifier = llm.with_structured_output(Decision)  # forces a typed answer


def classify(state: EmailState) -> dict:
    prompt = (
        "Triage this business email as respond, notify or ignore.\n"
        f"From: {state['sender']}\nSubject: {state['subject']}\n\n{state['body']}"
    )
    d = classifier.invoke(prompt)
    return {"category": d.category, "reason": d.reason}


def draft_reply(state: EmailState) -> dict:
    reply = llm.invoke(f"Write a short, polite reply to: {state['body']}")
    return {"action": f"DRAFT: {reply.content}"}  # Step 7 adds human review here


def notify(state: EmailState) -> dict:
    return {"action": f"NOTIFY team: {state['subject']}"}


def route(state: EmailState) -> str:
    return {"respond": "draft_reply", "notify": "notify"}.get(state["category"], END)


builder = StateGraph(EmailState)
builder.add_node("classify", classify)
builder.add_node("draft_reply", draft_reply)
builder.add_node("notify", notify)
builder.add_edge(START, "classify")
builder.add_conditional_edges("classify", route, ["draft_reply", "notify", END])
builder.add_edge("draft_reply", END)
builder.add_edge("notify", END)

# No checkpointer: the Agent Server handles persistence automatically.
graph = builder.compile()

"""Daily report agent: started by a cron job every morning at 8 AM IST."""
from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.tools import tool


@tool
def get_open_tickets() -> list[dict]:
    """Return open support tickets. Replace with your helpdesk API call."""
    return [
        {"id": "T-101", "customer": "Acme", "priority": "high", "age_days": 3},
        {"id": "T-117", "customer": "Zenith", "priority": "low", "age_days": 1},
    ]


@tool
def get_overdue_invoices() -> list[dict]:
    """Return overdue invoices. Replace with your accounts API call."""
    return [{"id": "INV-204", "amount_inr": 125000, "days_overdue": 12}]


# create_agent returns a compiled LangGraph graph, so the server can run it.
# Do not pass a checkpointer here: the Agent Server provides persistence.
agent = create_agent(
    model="openai:gpt-4.1-mini",
    tools=[get_open_tickets, get_overdue_invoices],
    system_prompt=(
        "You write a short morning operations report for an Indian business. "
        "Always call both tools, then give three sections: Tickets, Invoices, "
        "Top 3 actions for today. Use INR for money."
    ),
)

"""Create, list and disable the daily report cron on the Agent Server.

Usage: python scripts/crons.py create | list | disable <cron_id> | delete <cron_id>
"""
import asyncio
import os
import sys

from langgraph_sdk import get_client

client = get_client(url=os.getenv("AGENT_SERVER_URL", "http://localhost:2024"))
CALLBACK = os.getenv("CALLBACK_URL", "http://localhost:8000/run-done")


async def create() -> None:
    cron = await client.crons.create(
        "daily_report",               # assistant_id: the graph name works as default assistant
        schedule="0 8 * * *",         # min hour day month weekday -> 08:00 daily
        timezone="Asia/Kolkata",      # IANA name; without it, this would be 08:00 UTC
        input={"messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Write today's report."}]},
        webhook=CALLBACK,             # completion webhook: called when each run finishes
        on_run_completed="keep",      # keep each new thread so you can read old reports
    )
    print("created", cron["cron_id"])


async def list_crons() -> None:
    for c in await client.crons.search(assistant_id="daily_report"):
        print(c["cron_id"], c["schedule"], "enabled=", c.get("enabled"), "next=", c.get("next_run_date"))


async def disable(cron_id: str) -> None:
    await client.crons.update(cron_id, enabled=False)  # pause, keep the definition
    print("disabled", cron_id)


async def delete(cron_id: str) -> None:
    await client.crons.delete(cron_id)  # remove for good
    print("deleted", cron_id)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    cmd = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "list"
    if cmd == "create":
        asyncio.run(create())
    elif cmd == "list":
        asyncio.run(list_crons())
    elif cmd == "disable":
        asyncio.run(disable(sys.argv[2]))
    elif cmd == "delete":
        asyncio.run(delete(sys.argv[2]))
    else:
        sys.exit(__doc__)

"""Webhook service.
/incoming-email : event trigger from your mail provider -> starts a triage run.
/run-done       : completion webhook the Agent Server calls when a run ends.
"""
import os

from fastapi import FastAPI
from langgraph_sdk import get_client
from pydantic import BaseModel

AGENT_SERVER_URL = os.getenv("AGENT_SERVER_URL", "http://localhost:2024")
CALLBACK_URL = os.getenv("CALLBACK_URL", "http://localhost:8000/run-done")

app = FastAPI(title="ambient-inbox-automation")
client = get_client(url=AGENT_SERVER_URL)


class Email(BaseModel):
    sender: str
    subject: str
    body: str


@app.post("/incoming-email")
async def incoming_email(email: Email) -> dict:
    # One thread per email keeps each triage isolated and resumable.
    thread = await client.threads.create(metadata={"sender": email.sender})
    # Background run: returns at once; the server's task queue does the work.
    run = await client.runs.create(
        thread["thread_id"],
        "triage",                    # assistant_id from langgraph.json
        input=email.model_dump(),    # matches EmailState keys
        webhook=CALLBACK_URL,        # call us back when the run finishes
    )
    return {"thread_id": thread["thread_id"], "run_id": run["run_id"], "status": run["status"]}


@app.post("/run-done")
async def run_done(payload: dict) -> dict:
    # Payload is the finished run: ids, status and final values.
    print("RUN DONE:", payload.get("run_id"), payload.get("status"))
    values = payload.get("values") or {}
    if "action" in values:            # triage result
        print("TRIAGE:", values.get("category"), "->", values["action"])
    elif values.get("messages"):     # daily report from the cron
        print("REPORT:", values["messages"][-1].get("content"))
    return {"ok": True}
